# Overflow.project() reads a destroyed owner as live and logs its teardown as a defect

## Context

During a Workstation pop-out, the App worker logs `Neo.tab.plugin.Overflow: project() threw against a live owner Symbol(Neo.isDestroyed)` (`src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs`, the `project()` catch). The `workerErrors` auto-fixture (`test/playwright/fixtures.mjs:138`) fails any test whose page console receives it.

Observed:
- `WorkstationPopOutPaneIdentityNL.spec.mjs:205` was red on both attempts of the retry in [dev run 38313618683](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38313618683). It failed 1/3 on a hosted check (run 38315848558) with this exact error.
- `WorkstationReopenedPopupReturnNL.spec.mjs:125-128` already allowlists the same line as defect observation `a93f3f742aff4b33`. It was never promoted to a ticket. This is the second spec it fails, which meets the promotion rule.
- A [hosted probe](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38318164876) logged state from the catch, and it failed 1 of 6. At that failure, the owner `neo-tab-header-toolbar-9` is **destroyed**, and so is the plugin. The only measured button is destroyed too, and there is no control. The owner was not live: it was destroyed and still read `mounted: true`.

## The Problem

The catch decides "live owner" from `owner.mounted && !isWindowDeparted(owner.windowId)`. Destruction does not reset `mounted`, so a destroyed owner passes that test. Its own teardown, the projection rejecting with `Neo.isDestroyed`, is then logged as a programming defect. Every journey that destroys a tab header mid-projection either fails or must allowlist the line.

## The Architectural Reality

- The catch in `src/tab/plugin/Overflow.mjs` `project()` asks about two forms of departure: the owner unmounting, and its window retiring its port. A third, the owner or the plugin being destroyed, is not asked about. The `finally` releases the latch.
- `core.Base#destroy` rejects every trapped await with `Neo.isDestroyed`, and `component.Base#destroy` settles parked render promises the same way.

Design authority: the catch's own comment. A throw against a **live** owner is a defect, and a teardown race is the expected failure. A destroyed owner or plugin is torn down, not live.

## The Fix

The catch's live-owner test also requires that neither the plugin nor its owner is destroyed. Every other throw against a mounted, undestroyed owner in an undeparted window is still logged. Remove the allowlist in `WorkstationReopenedPopupReturnNL.spec.mjs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A receipt names the destroyed instances: the owner and the plugin ([run 38318164876](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/actions/runs/38318164876)).
- [ ] A unit arm in `test/playwright/unit/tab/plugin/Overflow.spec.mjs`, red before the fix, proves both directions. A projection that throws after its owner or plugin is destroyed logs nothing, even though `mounted` still reads true. A throw against an undestroyed, mounted owner is still logged.
- [ ] The allowlist line in `WorkstationReopenedPopupReturnNL.spec.mjs` is removed, and that spec passes on a hosted run.
- [ ] Post-merge: `WorkstationPopOutPaneIdentityNL:205` passes in the next ten-shard `dev` run.

## Out of Scope

- The other allowlisted line in that spec, `CanvasGroups: window … belongs to no canvas group`.
- Whether `destroy()` should reset `mounted`. That is an engine-wide change; this catch must not depend on it.
- The rest of #19657's intermittent set.

## Related
